lots.title: Provision of Fire Risk Assessments
lots.description: Provision of Fire Risk Assessments (FRAs) across the London Borough of Bexley's operational estate, including corporate buildings and multi-occupied residential buildings where in scope. Services encompass annual planning and scheduling, Type 1–4 surveys and Person-Centred FRAs, external wall appraisals (PAS 9980 FRAEW) where required, fire compartmentation support, and reporting via the Council's TF Cloud CAFM system. Contract term is 2 years with an option to extend up to 12 months (maximum 3 years).
requirements: Deliver FRAs to the scope instructed in strict accordance with the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 (as amended by the Fire Safety Act 2021 and Section 156 of the Building Safety Act 2022).
Provide all expertise, staff, labour, materials and equipment required to undertake FRAs in compliance with the cited legislative framework.
Individual assessors must hold recognised Fire Risk Assessment qualifications and be listed on the IFE Assessor Register (Associate Membership of IFE alone is not sufficient).
The Supplier organisation must hold BAFE SP205 certification or an equivalent UKAS-accredited scheme.
Comply with BS ISO 19706:2007 guidelines for assessing fire threat to people.

Develop an annual schedule of FRAs in collaboration with the Council, aligned to Appendix 1 – Bexley Fire Risk Assessment Price Matrix, and clearly distinguish statutory compliance activities from best-practice servicing activities.
Accommodate changes to the timing of site visits requested by the Council without incurring additional costs.
Where housing or mixed-use residential buildings fall in scope, align survey type to risk using the Type 1–4 approach and provide Person-Centred FRAs (PCFRA) for residents requiring support.
For external walls, determine whether a PAS 9980:2022 Fire Risk Appraisal of External Walls (FRAEW) is required and coordinate any specialist inputs.

For multi-occupied residential buildings, comply with the Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022, including quarterly common-parts fire door checks, annual flat entrance door checks, and (for high-rise) information boxes, floor plans, lift checks and wayfinding signage.

Issue FRA reports within 10 working days of site completion; reports must describe methodology and scope, significant findings, persons at risk, preventative/protective measures, aids to evacuation, a prioritised action plan, flags where further investigation is required, and include photographic evidence and plan mark-ups where available.
Report format must be compatible with the Council's TF Cloud CAFM system; upload status and documentation in agreed formats.
Submit anonymised sample FRAs (one standard FRA and one intrusive FRA) with explanatory notes as part of the tender response.
Propose risk-based review intervals and trigger reviews after material changes (occupancy, layout, systems) or following fire incidents/near misses.
Complete a mandatory Dynamic Risk Assessment (DRA) prior to any planned or reactive work and upload to TF Cloud or provide in an agreed format.

Support fire compartmentation surveys including intrusive works when instructed, coordinating joint visits with the Council's M&E and building fabric contractors and ensuring access to roof spaces and concealed areas.

Cease work immediately and notify the Council if asbestos is discovered or suspected; comply fully with the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 and site-specific Asbestos Risk Management Plans; assume the presence of ACMs in plant rooms and building fabric unless confirmed otherwise.

Appoint a Contract Manager as primary point of contact, attend monthly operational meetings and quarterly contract performance partnership meetings, and submit monthly, quarterly and annual reports covering service performance, asset changes, risks and mitigations, staffing, and financial summaries.
Comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, associated statutory instruments, HSE Guidance and ACOPs, including RIDDOR 2013 reporting obligations.
Ensure all staff (including subcontractors) have undergone appropriate DBS checks; maintain up-to-date records available to the Council on request.
Provide all equipment, safe power provision, and appropriate PPE; maintain comprehensive training and competency records and submit annually or on request.
Submit Risk Assessments and Method Statements (RAMS) for Council approval prior to commencing work; maintain and upload Workplace Risk Assessments to TF Cloud.

Any subcontracting requires prior Council approval following a technical and capability assessment; subcontractors must meet the same contractual terms and be DBS-checked; monitor subcontracted work via KPIs, spot checks and management oversight.

Comply with the Council's Environmental Policy where practicable; submit the Company Environmental Policy with practical implementation examples and alignment to the Council's Social Value priorities.

Operate a formal complaints procedure (submitted with tender response); log all complaints, report to the FM Client Unit within 24 hours with remedial action, and rectify service failures within agreed SLA timeframes.
Replacement personnel deployed within 5 working days where the Council requests removal of staff who fail performance standards or breach the Code of Conduct.
Issue signed Confidentiality Agreements to all Supplier staff and enforce Council site access, sign-in, identification and No Smoking policies.

During mobilisation, agree report templates (including alignment to BS 9792 where applicable), resource plan, programme, KPIs, TF Cloud data fields and information exchange protocols (including Section 156 FSO record-keeping duties).
Reference BS EN 1838:2024 for emergency lighting, BS 5839 (relevant parts) for fire detection and alarm systems, and BS 9991:2024 for strategies relying on evacuation lifts or EVC.

Other lots (Water Risk Assessments, Asbestos Assessments, Fire Door Surveys, etc.) are not emitted from this extraction.

This is a services contract (FRA delivery). product_requirement_seeds describe service-deliverable categories rather than goods SKUs; downstream product-matching logic should treat these as service-scope seeds, not goods.

The specification references 'Appendix 1 – Bexley Fire Risk Assessment Price Matrix' and an indicative property schedule in 'Appendix 1.2', neither of which is present in this extraction packet. Quantity hints are therefore qualitative.
